gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the BLUETTI AC180 has an ECO mode that switches the AC (or DC) output off when the load stays low for a set time. BLUETTI's manual puts the AC threshold anywhere from 15 to 30 W and the DC threshold from 5 to 10 W, with a delay of 1, 2, 3 or 4 hours. So a blanket on a low setting, or a 12 V blanket, can lose power partway through the night unless ECO is turned off.
standout_why: I read the three cited pages: dealectric.com (our current page), blackoutwise.com (Jackery 1000 v2 + blanket) and wattfort.com, plus runtimemath.com, which ranked #2. All four only change Wh into hours, each using a 0.85 factor. Runtimemath also subtracts the station's own draw (AC180 15 W). Wattfort covers the blanket's auto-off timer and Sunbeam's ban on inverters. None of them says that the station's own low-load auto-off can end the night early, and none gives a threshold for any station. WattFort says outright that it gives no AC auto-off or eco-mode behaviour for any station, and BlackoutWise and RuntimeMath say nothing about it either.
decides: The AC180 stays the pick: it is $499 and in stock at BLUETTI today, has 1,152 Wh, and the blanket counts as the resistive load its manual describes. The finding adds a condition to that pick: turn ECO off, or set it to its lowest threshold, before using the AC180 overnight. Thermostat-controlled blankets on low and 12 V blankets on the car port are the loads most likely to sit under 15–30 W (AC) or 5–10 W (DC) for an hour or more. Because the hour figures are rated-capacity arithmetic, a station that shuts off at hour 3 never reaches them. The same check should go in the table for every candidate. I could not source the default thresholds for the AC180, or the energy-saving thresholds for the Jackery 1000 v2, so the page should show that column as manual-stated ranges, not defaults.

findings.label: ECO mode (auto-off on low load)
findings.value: AC and DC output turn off when load stays low; AC threshold 15–30 W, DC threshold 5–10 W, delay 1, 2, 3 or 4 h
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 User Manual, p.14 (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: Manual text: 'When operating on ECO mode, the AC/DC output will automatically turn off if the AC180 is bearing low or no load for a while.' The table on the page lists Power '15W-30W' and '5W-10W' and Duration '1, 2, 3, 4 hours'. Its column headers are missing on the mirror. Reading the first column as AC and the second as DC matches a BLUETTI manual summary found in search, but I did not open that summary page myself. ECO is toggled with the DC power button in Setting mode. The page does not say whether ECO is on by default.

findings.label: Continuous vs resistive-load (Power Lifting) output
findings.value: 1,800 W rated; up to 2,700 W for pure resistive loads in Power Lifting mode, which is off by default and not available while charging from AC
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 User Manual, p.13 (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: A heated blanket is a pure resistive load, the kind the manual's footnote describes (heating elements). Any blanket is far below 1,800 W, so this figure does not limit the pick. I include it to put BLUETTI's surge figure on the same basis as the others.

findings.label: Car outlet rating
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 User Manual, p.12 (ManualsLib copy)
findings.note: '12VDC/10A' appears in the spec table, but the layout on the mirror is scrambled, so it is only probably the car-outlet row. 120 W is my arithmetic (12 V × 10 A). That covers the 50 W / 4.2 A KickAss 12 V blanket WattFort cites.

findings.label: Price and stock, BLUETTI US store
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC180 Solar Portable Power Station | 1,800W 1,152Wh
findings.note: Read from the Shopify product JSON with storecheck.py; this is the price of the 'AC180 | 1800W, 1152Wh' variant, compare-at also $499.00. Our page says stock is 'Back late Nov'. That is out of date: the variant shows as available today.

findings.label: Usable-capacity factor the rival pages use
findings.value: 0.85 × rated Wh on all three (BlackoutWise: Jackery 1000 v2 1,070 Wh → 'about 910 Wh usable'; RuntimeMath also subtracts the station's own draw, e.g. AC180 15 W)
findings.source_title: Jackery 1000 v2 + Electric Blanket: About 1 Night per Charge
findings.note: WattFort (https://wattfort.com/guides/power-station-electric-blanket/) and RuntimeMath (https://runtimemath.com/how-long-will-a-power-station-run-an-electric-blanket) also use 0.85; both read 2026-11-14. BlackoutWise says it does not test units and that its 12 h is 'an estimate, not a measured result'. None of these pages accounts for a station switching itself off.

findings.product: Jackery Explorer 1000 (manual mirror, model not confirmed as v2)
findings.label: Energy Saving Mode shutdown
findings.value: Whole unit shuts down after 12 h with no charging input or discharging output; toggle by long-pressing the AC and main power buttons
findings.note: The mirror does not say whether this is the v2, and it gives no low-load wattage threshold. Use it only as a pointer, not as a v2 spec.
